title: Oscar and the Kitchen
premise: Vesper Galloway, a lighthouse keeper's grandson and part-time novelist, has spent three years hiding from the scandal that ended his engagement and nearly closed his family's bakery. When his sister begs him to bring a date to the Galloway reunion, he hires Oscar Reyes, a charming stranger from the diner next door, to play pretend for one weekend. But Oscar's easy warmth cracks Vesper's armor faster than any real courtship could, and by dessert Vesper realizes his safe, invisible life was just another way of punishing himself. As the bakery lease expires and the truth about who really betrayed whom three years ago surfaces, Vesper must choose between protecting his pride and claiming the love—and the life—waiting in plain sight.
about_author: Coral Whitlock is the pen name of a former pastry chef who traded early mornings at the oven for late nights at the keyboard, writing love stories set in small coastal towns where everyone knows your order. She lives in a converted lighthouse cottage with her partner and an opinionated cat named Crumb.

chapters.title: The Stranger at Table Six
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Three years after public humiliation ended his engagement, Vesper runs the failing Galloway Bakery and writes novels no one reads. When his sister demands a date for the family reunion, he impulsively asks Oscar, the regular who always orders the same scone. The emotional beat: cautious hope flickering through self-protective numbness as they strike a deal over cooling racks.

chapters.title: Reunion Weather
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the windswept reunion, Oscar plays the boyfriend so well it unsettles them both—until Vesper's ex appears with the man who actually spread the rumors that ruined him. Oscar watches Vesper shrink into old shame and quietly defends him in front of everyone. The emotional beat: tenderness turning protective, the fake date feeling dangerously real by dessert.

chapters.title: What the Lighthouse Saw
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm strands Oscar at the bakery overnight, and Vesper finally confesses the truth: his ex didn't betray him—he let Vesper take the blame to protect his own reputation, and Vesper agreed out of loyalty. Oscar challenges him to stop paying for someone else's sin before the lease runs out. The emotional beat: raw vulnerability, the first honest kiss, then fear of exposure driving Vesper to push Oscar away.

chapters.title: Rising Dough
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. On the lease's final day, Oscar publicly tells the reunion crowd the truth Vesper couldn't, forcing Vesper to forgive the man in the mirror. Vesper signs a new lease, publishes under his own name, and asks Oscar for a real first date. The emotional beat: cathartic release—loyalty to truth wins, love stops being a performance, and the bakery reopens full of light.
